title: Activation Keywords / Scan Depth entirely absent — the direct answer to the skill's own cost warning
reality: Custom agents support Activation Keywords: up to 100 keywords/phrases (customAgentActivationSettingsSchema in agent.schema.ts) plus activationScanDepth (DEFAULT_CUSTOM_AGENT_ACTIVATION_SCAN_DEPTH = 5, MAX = 200, per packages/shared/src/constants/agent-activation.ts). The agent then runs ONLY when a keyword appears in that many recent messages; an empty keyword box means run every time on the normal cadence. Documented in docs/agents/custom-agents.md 'Activation Keywords'. Neither SKILL.md nor references/agents.md mentions this anywhere.
fix: Add an 'Activation Keywords (cost control)' subsection to the Custom Agents section of references/agents.md, and reference it from the ideation anti-pattern "I'll build everything as custom agents" in SKILL.md and from decision-guide.md Q5. This is high severity: the skill repeatedly warns that custom agents fire every turn and cost tokens, then never names the built-in mitigation. The correct advice is keyword-gate the agent, not drop it.

title: Named prompt options / Prompt Mode variants undocumented
reality: A single custom agent can hold several named prompt variants ('Named prompt options'). Each chat then picks one via a Prompt Mode dropdown without editing the agent globally; if no options are defined the chat menu shows only the default prompt. Documented in docs/agents/custom-agents.md. references/agents.md matches the string 'Prompt Mode' only in an unrelated context.
fix: Document in references/agents.md's Custom Agents section. Architecturally relevant: it is the supported way to get per-chat behavioral variation from ONE agent, and should be recommended instead of cloning an agent per variant — which the skill currently has no answer for.

title: 'Add as Prompt Section' output-exposure toggle missing
reality: Custom agents have an 'Add as Prompt Section' setting that exposes the agent's latest output as a section injectable in a prompt preset (docs/agents/custom-agents.md, 'Other settings you can adjust').
fix: Add to references/agents.md. This is the documented bridge between an agent's output and prompt assembly — directly relevant to the skill's claim that prompt assembly is not user-extensible, which is too absolute without this caveat.

title: Agent Budget defaults confirmed from user docs (corroborates pass B)
reality: docs/agents/custom-agents.md 'Other settings you can adjust' states Context Size default 5 and Max Output Tokens default 4096, range 128 to 32768 — independently matching the constants in packages/shared/src/types/agent.ts.
fix: Same fix as the pass-B Agent Budget finding: add an Agent Budget subsection to references/agents.md with both defaults and the range.

title: Cached prompt injections panel undocumented
reality: docs/agents/approvals-and-agent-suite.md documents a 'Cached prompt injections panel' alongside the Agent Write Approval modal and Character Card Update review. references/agents.md covers the Agent Suite but not the cached-injections surface.
fix: Add a short note to the Agent Suite subsection of references/agents.md. Useful for debugging 'why is this agent's old output still in my prompt', which is otherwise an unanswerable question from the current references.

title: Memory Recall vs Chat Summary split not clearly mapped
reality: docs/agents/memory.md frames Marinara as having 'two memory systems' — Memory Recall (embedding-based, per-chat, with its own embedding source) and Chat Summary (Roleplay). With Long-Term Memory now a catalog package and recalledMemories a custom-agent context source, three related concepts now exist and the references do not draw the boundary in one place.
fix: Add a short 'Three memory surfaces' orientation block to references/agents.md or architecture.md: Memory Recall (built-in embedding retrieval), Chat Summary (condensed history, now with multi-select condensation in v2.4.0), and the Long-Term Memory package — plus which of them the recalledMemories context source actually feeds.
